packet.answer:
Bringing a lamp to the repair café? Please use the side door and arrive by 6 p.m. Friday.

I changed “the usual entrance” to “the side door” because a first-time visitor wouldn’t know which entrance we usually use.
packet.displayed: “The side door” gives a first-time visitor a specific entrance to look for, and “by 6 p.m. Friday” tells them when to arrive. Your explanation shows why the edit matters: the visitor can act on the notice without knowing the café’s routine. For practice, rewrite the notice for a first-time volunteer using the same brief. Which detail would you change, and what would you need to ask before giving the volunteer an arrival time?
packet.evidence_limit: Review covers the submitted passage and its editing rationale. Several voices and arrangements can serve the same reader. Whether real readers understood it needs a reader observation. Fiction, poetry, the learner's overall talent and any private writing remain outside this finding.
packet.goal: I want to learn how to be a better writer
packet.learner: I almost added “Volunteers use the main entrance” because I pictured a visitor seeing people go in there and following them. I left it out because I pictured my notice taped beside the main door, where the lamp instruction would be the first thing they saw. Yes, please save writing clear directions for first-time readers as a topic.

material.excerpt: A regular knows what 'the usual place' means. A newcomer needs a place they can identify. Ask what that reader has to do next. Choose the facts that make it possible and keep the voice your own.
material.lesson: Before you polish a draft, imagine handing it to one person. What are they trying to do? Underline a phrase that makes them borrow knowledge from a regular. Replace it with a fact the brief actually gives you. Read the new line in your own voice.

packet.policy: Help with the current task and then offer practice.
packet.task: A repair café needs a notice for a first-time visitor bringing a lamp. Visitors bringing a lamp use the side door by 6 p.m. Friday. Volunteers use the main entrance. The draft reads, 'Please come to the usual entrance by the deadline.' Write your version for that visitor, then explain one edit in terms of what the reader needs. Choose your own voice.

response.display: Your choice fits the spot you pictured. Beside the main door, the notice tells a first-time visitor with a lamp where to go next. If the notice were farther away and the visitor saw volunteers entering first, ‘Volunteers use the main entrance’ could help them understand why they should head to the side door. Try writing a version for that spot using only facts from the brief. I’ve noted ‘Writing clear directions for first-time readers’ as your revisit topic here.
